incidents.vector: Self-propagating npm worm steals developer and CI/CD credentials, then abuses trusted-publishing OIDC workflows to push trojanized package updates under maintainer accounts.
incidents.impact: At least 373 malicious package versions across 169 npm names confirmed (mainly TanStack); evidence of comparable scale across SAP packages, AI tooling, and enterprise libraries. Heavily obfuscated JavaScript and Bun-based execution evade Node.js-focused defenses.

incidents.vector: Initial access in September 2020 via a malicious email attachment; attacker persisted for nearly two years and exploited unpatched ZeroLogon to escalate to a domain administrator account, moving freely across an environment with only 5% SOC coverage.
incidents.impact: UK ICO fined the company £963,900 ($1.3M) on May 11. The 2022 Cl0p-linked breach exposed 633,887 customers' and employees' personal data (4.1 TB published), including bank details, NI numbers, and disability indicators. No operational technology was impacted.

incidents.vector: Phishing and malvertising campaigns plus a planted fake SourceForge project distributed malicious installers posing as aviation software; multi-stage infection chained a JavaScript RAT, PowerShell, and an LNK shortcut exploit (ZDI-CAN-25373).
incidents.impact: Threat actor 'HeartlessSoul' (also tracked as Versatile Werewolf) is exfiltrating GIS shape files, digital terrain models, GPS data, and proprietary aviation files used to model adversary terrain awareness. Campaign active since at least September 2025.

incidents.victim: Open-source web administration tool users (vendor undisclosed)
incidents.vector: AI-developed Python zero-day script that bypasses two-factor authentication on a popular open-source admin tool; Google identified LLM hallmarks (hallucinated CVSS score, structured docstrings) in the exploit code.
incidents.impact: First documented case of a cybercrime group weaponizing an AI-built zero-day. Google GTIG disclosed the flaw to the vendor before a planned mass-exploitation campaign by a 'well-known' threat group could launch; vulnerability patched.

incidents.vector: AI virtual training platform left an API exposed online without authentication for approximately 150 days before remediation.
incidents.impact: Service member records and sensitive military training documents exposed; discovered and disclosed by security firm Strix. No malicious access has been confirmed.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure and may have accessed the customer API key database.
incidents.impact: Customers — including Cloudflare, Vercel, Stripe, and other tech giants — were instructed to rotate API keys. Downstream risk to enterprise AI observability deployments and key material.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a flaw in Canvas Free-for-Teacher accounts to gain unauthorized access; the same flaw was re-exploited a week after Instructure said the incident was contained, allowing defacement of the Canvas login page across ~330 institutions.
incidents.impact: Canvas was taken offline mid-finals across US schools; usernames, email addresses, student IDs, and user messages were stolen. Instructure paid the extortion demand and says it received digital confirmation (shred logs) of data destruction. The House Homeland Security Committee opened an inquiry.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated buffer overflow (CVE-2026-0300) in the User-ID Authentication Portal allowed shellcode injection into an nginx worker process; attackers then deployed tunneling tools (EarthWorm, ReverseSocks5) and used a SAML flood to pivot to a second device.
incidents.impact: At least one PA-Series firewall fully compromised at root; attackers conducted Active Directory enumeration against domain root using firewall service-account credentials, destroyed logs, and removed evidence. Unit 42 tracks the cluster as CL-STA-1132; limited exploitation observed to date.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools users (selected targets in Russia, Belarus, Thailand)
incidents.vector: AVB Disc Soft's distribution site was compromised; trojanized DAEMON Tools installers signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate have shipped since at least April 8 and beacon host data to attacker infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Thousands of infections globally, but second-stage QUIC RAT was deployed only to about a dozen carefully selected targets at government, scientific, manufacturing, and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus, and Thailand — consistent with a targeted Chinese-speaking espionage operation.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Initial access likely via zero-day or n-day exploits, followed by deployment of multiple China-linked malware families (NetDraft, CloudSorcerer v3, SNAPPYBEE, ZingDoor, Draculoader) and open-source tools (Impacket) for credential extraction and lateral movement.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos confirms cluster UAT-8302 has been active against South American government targets since late 2024 and southeastern European agencies in 2025, maintaining long-term access for intelligence collection.

incidents.vector: Attacker breached the corporate network on May 4, exfiltrated data, and deployed ransomware that encrypted systems supporting shipping, receiving, and manufacturing.
incidents.impact: Pennsylvania-based maker of injectable drug packaging (10,000+ employees, $3B+ revenue) disclosed the breach in an SEC 8-K. Global business operations temporarily disrupted; core enterprise systems restored but full restoration timeline not finalized. Unit 42 leading investigation; no ransomware gang has claimed responsibility yet.

incidents.vector: Social-engineering attack against DigiCert tech support staff — attacker posed as a customer and tricked employees into running a malicious Windows screensaver (.SCR) file; a misconfigured CrowdStrike EDR agent failed to alert for nearly two weeks.
incidents.impact: 27 EV code-signing certificates stolen and used to sign Zhong Stealer malware, a family previously linked to Chinese e-crime group GoldenEyeDog (APT-Q-27). All 60 in-flight EV certificates from the compromise window were revoked.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed Trellix source code repositories; the company says no product changes were made and that it notified law enforcement. Given Trellix's role as a close Europol partner, the exposure is sensitive even without product tampering.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised an admin account and set the delay on admin actions to zero, executing malicious transactions across multiple integrated blockchains instantly.
incidents.impact: Approximately $5 million in crypto assets stolen from the cross-chain trading platform.

incidents.vector: Sustained, multi-day distributed denial-of-service attacks against Canonical domains and APIs, attributed to a pro-Palestinian hacktivist group that previously DDoSed Bluesky and Mastodon.
incidents.impact: Users were unable to install or update Ubuntu OS for days; web infrastructure supporting one of the world's most-used Linux distributions remained degraded. The same group is also being sued by Chime customers over an April DDoS.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the embassy's Microsoft Exchange email server as part of a larger 2026 campaign that has hit more than 5,000 Exchange servers globally.
incidents.impact: Cuban diplomatic email inboxes were stolen, providing Beijing visibility into Havana's communications regarding the US naval blockade of Iran and broader Caribbean diplomacy.

incidents.victim: Web hosting customers via cPanel/WHM (incl. Guam government)
incidents.vector: Authentication bypass and remote code execution in cPanel/WHM (CVE-2026-41940, affecting all versions after 11.40); attackers wipe public sites and post fake $8,000 Bitcoin ransom demands. The same flaw is also being used to deploy cryptominers and DDoS malware.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver counts more than 44,000 compromised cPanel systems; thousands of sites defaced. Guam government sites were taken offline. Australian ACSC issued a critical alert; no ransom payments observed in the attacker wallet.

incidents.vector: Specific vectors withheld; attackers gained access to industrial control systems at some of the five impacted facilities.
incidents.impact: Five Polish water treatment stations were hacked over the past year; Poland's intelligence service (ABW) confirmed the incidents but has not attributed them to any group or state. No public reports of disruption to water service.

incidents.vector: Specific access path not publicly disclosed; CNAM's national database was breached and no ransom demand was made — a pattern Moldovan officials associate with state-aligned activity.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial data of essentially every adult Moldovan citizen, plus private medical providers' financial details, were stolen; about 30% of records were impacted (stolen and/or restored from backups). Moldovan cyber authorities have not ruled out Russian involvement amid escalating tensions over Transnistria.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; the 'World Leaks' hacking group exfiltrated internal data and listed Mediaworks on its data leak site.
incidents.impact: Leaked internal meeting notes document Mediaworks editorial directors coordinating with Moscow on anti-Ukraine content placement. Mediaworks is suing publishers that reported on the leak; Hungary's pro-Kremlin party lost the April national elections.

incidents.industry: Multi-industry (Healthcare, Financial services, Professional services, Technology)
incidents.vector: Multi-stage 'code of conduct' phishing campaign using polished HTML lures, PDF attachments, and CAPTCHA-gated landing pages on attacker-controlled .de domains; final stage proxied a real Microsoft sign-in to capture authentication tokens (AiTM), bypassing non-phishing-resistant MFA.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Research observed waves between April 14 and 16 targeting predominantly US recipients (92%); compromised accounts grant immediate persistent access via stolen tokens. Notable for use of legitimate email delivery services and the 'Paubox' encryption branding to bolster credibility.

incidents.vector: Specifics not disclosed; ransomware attack on April 8 affected municipal IT systems.
incidents.impact: City of Ardmore suffered a ransomware attack early last month; impact details have not been publicly enumerated beyond the initial disclosure.
